question.problem:
Consider the following trigonometric equation:

$$
\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{x}{2}+\frac{\pi }{6})=-\sqrt{2}
$$

The general solution of this equation is

$$
x=\frac{7\pi }{6}+4\pi n,\,x=a+4\pi n,
$$

where $n$ is any integer. Which of the following could be the value of $a?$
question.worked_solution:
First, note that the given equation is equivalent to

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{x}{2}+\frac{\pi }{6})=-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.
$$

Therefore, the general solution to our equation is

$$
\frac{x}{2}+\frac{\pi }{6}=\frac{3\pi }{4}+2\pi n,\,\frac{x}{2}+\frac{\pi }{6}=\frac{5\pi }{4}+2\pi n.
$$

Solving the two equations above for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{2}=-\frac{\pi }{6}+\frac{3\pi }{4}+2\pi n, & \,\frac{x}{2}=-\frac{\pi }{6}+\frac{5\pi }{4}+2\pi n \\ \frac{x}{2}=\frac{7\pi }{12}+2\pi n, & \,\frac{x}{2}=\frac{13\pi }{12}+2\pi n \\ x=\frac{7\pi }{6}+4\pi n, & \,x=\frac{13\pi }{6}+4\pi n.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have that $a=\frac{13\pi }{6}.$
